items.text: Morgan Stanley states its broker-dealers are subject to the SEC's Regulation Best Interest, which requires them to act in the best interest of retail customers when making a recommendation without placing their own interests ahead of the customer's.
items.quote: the SEC's "Regulation Best Interest," which requires broker-dealers to act in the "best interest" of retail customers at the time a recommendation is made without placing the financial or other interests of the broker-dealer ahead of the interest of the retail customer.

items.text: Edward Jones states it is subject to the SEC rule requiring delivery of a Form CRS Relationship Summary informing clients of fees, costs, conflicts of interest, and disciplinary history.
items.quote: the SEC rule requiring registered investment advisers and broker-dealers to deliver a Form CRS Relationship Summary to their clients informing them of the types of client relationships offered, together with the applicable standards of care, and information on fees, costs, conflicts of interest, and legal and disciplinary history.

items.text: Raymond James states Regulation Best Interest and Form CRS required it to implement additional client disclosures and education, and that various states have proposed or adopted differing conduct standards.
items.quote: Regulation Best Interest requires a broker-dealer to act in the best interest of a retail client when making a recommendation... Form CRS requires that broker-dealers and investment advisers provide retail investors with a brief summary document... Various states have also proposed, or adopted, laws and regulations seeking to impose new standards of conduct on broker-dealers.

items.text: Raymond James states the UK FCA Consumer Duty, effective July 31, 2023, requires firms to deliver good outcomes for retail customers with respect to price and value, among other things.
items.quote: on July 31, 2023, the FCA's Consumer Duty took effect in the UK. Among other things, the UK Consumer Duty requires firms to act to deliver "good outcomes" for retail customers with respect to products and services, price and value, consumer understanding, and consumer support.

items.text: Raymond James states the DOL issued a final rule in April 2024 significantly expanding the definition of investment advice fiduciary under ERISA, which was stayed by federal courts.
items.quote: In April 2024, the Department of Labor ("DOL") issued a final rule significantly expanding the definition of "investment advice fiduciary" under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended... two federal district courts separately issued nationwide stays of the effective date.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that under DOL regulations under ERISA Section 408(b)(2), it must provide information on its services and compensation to fiduciaries to assess the reasonableness of compensation.
items.quote: In accordance with Department of Labor regulations under Section 408(b)(2) of ERISA, MSWM is required to provide certain information regarding our services and compensation to assist fiduciaries and plan sponsors... in assessing the reasonableness of their plan's contracts or arrangements with us, including the reasonableness of our compensation.

items.text: Merrill Lynch states that under DOL regulations under ERISA Section 408(b)(2), it must provide compensation information to fiduciaries and plan sponsors of retirement accounts to assess the reasonableness of compensation.
items.quote: In accordance with Department of Labor regulations under Section 408(b)(2) of ERISA, we are required to provide certain information regarding our services and compensation to assist fiduciaries and plan sponsors... in assessing the reasonableness of their plan's contracts or arrangements with us, including the reasonableness of our compensation.

items.text: Raymond James states that beginning August 2024 the SEC's Division of Enforcement requested information regarding its cash sweep program practices for advisory clients and has reportedly conducted similar reviews at other institutions.
items.quote: beginning in August 2024, the SEC's Division of Enforcement requested information regarding our practices related to cash sweep programs for investment advisory clients and has reportedly conducted similar reviews at other financial institutions.

items.text: Schwab states the SEC found it made false and misleading statements in Form ADV Part 2A brochures about cash allocations in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios accounts, including its conflict of interest in setting cash allocations.
items.quote: The SEC found that CS&Co. made false and misleading statements in Form ADV Part 2A brochures about the cash allocations in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios accounts, in particular about: CS&Co.'s conflict of interest in setting the cash allocations.

items.text: Merrill Lynch states the SEC issued an administrative order finding its wrap fee program disclosures contained a material misstatement because a production credit fee was charged but not disclosed alongside the disclosed currency mark-up.
items.quote: wrap fee advisory program agreements and ADV brochures contained a material misstatement because, while disclosing that MLPF&S charged a mark-up or markdown on foreign currency exchanges, the disclosure did not also state that an additional fee referred to as a production credit was also charged.

items.text: Schwab states that regulations governing broker-dealers cover, among other things, fee arrangements, order flow revenue, disclosure to clients, and fiduciary duties.
items.quote: The regulations cover all aspects of the securities business, including, among other things... fee arrangements, order flow revenue from securities exchanges and market makers, disclosure to clients, fiduciary duties, and the conduct of directors, officers, and employees.

items.text: A trade report states that under the SEC's Marketing Rule (Rule 206(4)-1), financial firms are legally exposed if they promote third-party ratings or badges that cannot be verified as completely impartial.
items.quote: Under the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) Marketing Rule (Rule 206(4)-1), financial firms are legally exposed if they promote third-party ratings or badges that cannot be verified as completely impartial.

items.text: Schwab states the SEC withdrew the proposed Order Competition Rule and Regulation Best Execution in June 2025, which the company had been evaluating.
items.quote: On June 12, 2025, the SEC withdrew certain notices of proposed rulemaking issued between March 2022 and November 2023, which the Company had been evaluating. The withdrawn proposals included the December 2022 equity market structure rule proposals, "Order Competition Rule" and "Regulation Best Execution".
